lede: Two days in AI is a long time. An always-on agent shipped, a funding round repriced what talent costs, and the operators spent the week arguing about what any of it means. Here is the last 48 hours, woven into one story.

sections.closing_take: The agent is becoming infrastructure. Bet on the plumbing, not the demo.

briefing.lede: The personal agent just grew a nervous system.
briefing.steal_this: Ask what in your product could run ambiently instead of on-demand. The answer is usually the most valuable part.
briefing.what_happened: OpenAI launched Dots, an always-on personal AI agent that runs in the background, watches what you're working on, and acts without being prompted.
briefing.why_it_matters: This is the interface disappearing. Every agent so far has been a chatbot you visit; Dots is a colleague that never leaves. If it works, the entire 'open the app and ask' paradigm looks quaint within a year.

items.title: OpenAI launches Dots, an always-on personal AI agent

sections.kicker: Agentic AI, last 48 hours — what moved and why it matters.
sections.narrative: The week's throughline is the agent going ambient. The launches that mattered weren't bigger models — they were agents that stay on, watch, and act without being asked. That is a different product category wearing the same clothes, and the teams shipping it are betting the interface disappears entirely.
sections.title: The Signal

sections.closing_take: Listen for the arguments, not the agreements.

briefing.lede: Attention is the new cap table.
briefing.steal_this: Whatever you're building, ask who already has your customer's attention. That's your distribution partner.
briefing.what_happened: Jake Paul joined the besties to talk about converting a massive audience into real businesses — the boxing playbook, and why politics might be next.
briefing.why_it_matters: Strip away the celebrity and the thesis is pure operator: distribution is the moat, and the people who own attention are quietly becoming the people who own equity.

sections.narrative: The circuit's theme this week was attention as capital — who has it, what it buys, and whether fame helps or hurts when you're allocating it. The operators are unusually candid about the gap between narrative and numbers right now.
